   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2018/2001 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 December 2018 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources (recast)», the European Union's renewable energy directive. A directive is a law addressed to governments, which each write it into national law; it reaches a business through that national law. Where it applies: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» Its subject: «This Directive establishes a common framework for the promotion of energy from renewable sources.»

The text read here is the Directive as adopted and printed in the Official Journal of the European Union. It holds no later amendment, so a change made to the Directive after adoption is not covered here. What the Directive says is quoted from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The text names no freight forwarder, so each statement about a forwarder's position is a reading and not something the text says. This document serves the regulatory and operational lenses from the Directive's own text. The text holds no market price, no tonnage figure and no research study, so it carries no market or research content.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

In plain terms, the Directive sets the European Union's rules for growing the share of renewable energy and, for transport, it works through the companies that sell fuel rather than through the companies that buy transport.

The Union goal: «It sets a binding Union target for the overall share of energy from renewable sources in the Union's gross final consumption of energy in 2030.» The binding figure: «Member States shall collectively ensure that the share of energy from renewable sources in the Union's gross final consumption of energy in 2030 is at least 32 %.» Each Member State also keeps a floor of its own: «From 1 January 2021, the share of energy from renewable sources in each Member State's gross final consumption of energy shall not be lower than the baseline share shown in the third column of the table in Part A of Annex I to this Directive.»

When it took effect (in force): «This Directive shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» It was adopted on «Done at Strasbourg, 11 December 2018.» The Directive counts the Commission's powers to adopt delegated acts from a fixed date: «shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 24 December 2018.» The earlier directive was repealed from a date that has passed: «Directive 2009/28/EC, as amended by the Directives listed in Part A of Annex X, is repealed with effect from 1 July 2021»

Why this reaches a freight business: for transport the share is not placed on the companies that move cargo. «each Member State shall set an obligation on fuel suppliers to ensure that the share of renewable energy within the final consumption of energy in the transport sector is at least 14 % by 2030 (minimum share) in accordance with an indicative trajectory set by the Member State and calculated in accordance with the methodology set out in this Article and in Articles 26 and 27.» The same article lets governments choose who is covered: «Member States may exempt, or distinguish between, different fuel suppliers and different energy carriers when setting the obligation on the fuel suppliers, ensuring that the varying degrees of maturity and the cost of different technologies are taken into account.»

*Analytical inference:* because the transport share is placed on fuel suppliers through national law, a freight business meets this Directive as a buyer of fuel and as a seller of transport that may carry a renewable-fuel claim, and not as the party that has to reach the share. The text states no price effect of the obligation, so any change to a fuel price or to what a customer is charged is not stated here; it depends on national rules and on supplier contracts that the text does not hold.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: nothing in the text puts a step on a freight business in the coming month. The nearest dated step is the Commission's own, a duty on the Commission and not on a freight business: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall assess whether the criteria laid down in paragraphs 6 and 7 effectively minimise the risk of using forest biomass derived from unsustainable production and address LULUCF criteria, on the basis of the available data. The Commission shall, if appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to amend the criteria laid down in paragraphs 6 and 7 for the period after 2030.» A second Commission assessment falls on the same date: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall assess the impact of such additional criteria on the internal market, accompanied, if necessary, by a proposal to ensure harmonisation thereof.»

- A fuel-procurement lead asks each fuel supplier, at the next supply-contract renewal, whether the fuel it sells counts toward the transport obligation set under national law and what proof of sustainability comes with it.
- A customer-claims lead holds back any statement to a customer that a shipment ran on renewable fuel until the supplier has given that proof, on the next quote that offers such a claim.
- A procurement lead records, on each supplier's proof, whether the feedstock is one of the Part B feedstocks of Annex IX that section 8 shows are limited, at the next supplier review.

*Analytical inference:* these steps rest on the supplier and operator duties quoted in section 8, which fall on fuel suppliers and economic operators; the Directive requires none of them of a freight business. The text states no penalty and no cost figure for such a business.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The parties the text names are the Member States, fuel suppliers, economic operators, voluntary schemes and verifiers, and the Commission. A forwarder is not named.

Fuel suppliers carry the transport share: «each Member State shall set an obligation on fuel suppliers to ensure that the share of renewable energy within the final consumption of energy in the transport sector is at least 14 % by 2030 (minimum share) in accordance with an indicative trajectory set by the Member State and calculated in accordance with the methodology set out in this Article and in Articles 26 and 27.» Fuel suppliers also feed the tracing database: «Fuel suppliers shall enter the information necessary to verify compliance with the requirements laid down in the first and fourth subparagraphs of Article 25(1) into the relevant database.» Economic operators carry the proof: «Member States shall require economic operators to show that the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in Article 29(2) to (7) and (10) have been fulfilled.» The proof must follow the fuel through the supply chain: «requires information about the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving characteristics and sizes of the consignments referred to in point (a) to remain assigned to the mixture;»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that buys fuel, or that sells a transport service with a renewable-fuel claim, sits downstream of the fuel supplier in this chain; the text does not place it in either named role. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that arranges fuel for a customer, or that sells a renewable-fuel claim, counts as an economic operator or as a fuel supplier under the national law that carries this Directive.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance document is held for this Directive.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets dated steps for the Commission. A date already passed is marked as passed; the text read here does not say whether each act was adopted or each report submitted, so the outcome of a passed step is not stated.

Steps ahead:
- Forest biomass criteria. «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall assess whether the criteria laid down in paragraphs 6 and 7 effectively minimise the risk of using forest biomass derived from unsustainable production and address LULUCF criteria, on the basis of the available data. The Commission shall, if appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to amend the criteria laid down in paragraphs 6 and 7 for the period after 2030.» What it changes for the reader: the assessment can lead to a Commission proposal to amend the criteria for biomass fuels for the period after 2030.
- Extra national criteria. «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall assess the impact of such additional criteria on the internal market, accompanied, if necessary, by a proposal to ensure harmonisation thereof.»
- Proposal for the period after 2030 (the text read here does not say whether it has been submitted). «In 2026, the Commission shall submit, if appropriate, a legislative proposal on the regulatory framework for the promotion of energy from renewable sources for the period after 2030.»
- Review report. «In 2032, the Commission shall publish a report reviewing the application of this Directive.»

Steps whose date has passed:
- Forest biomass evidence (date passed). «By 31 January 2021, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the operational guidance on the evidence for demonstrating compliance with the criteria laid down in paragraphs 6 and 7 of this Article.»
- Advanced biofuels obligation (date passed). «By 31 December 2025, in the context of the biennial assessment of progress made pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/1999, the Commission shall assess whether the obligation relating to advanced biofuels and biogas produced from feedstock listed in Part A of Annex IX laid down in the fourth subparagraph of Article 25(1) effectively stimulates innovation and ensures greenhouse gas emissions savings in the transport sector.»
- Feedstock list review, repeated every two years (first date passed). «By 25 June 2019 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall review the list of feedstock set out in Parts A and B of Annex IX with a view to adding feedstock in accordance with the principles set out in the third subparagraph.»
- Certification of low-risk fuels and a later review (dates passed). «By 1 February 2019, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 35 to supplement this Directive by setting out the criteria for certification of low indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels and for determining the high indirect land-use change-risk feedstock for which a significant expansion of the production area into land with high-carbon stock is observed.» «By 1 September 2023, the Commission shall review the criteria laid down in the delegated act referred to in the fourth subparagraph based on the best available scientific data and shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 35 to amend such criteria, where appropriate, and to include a trajectory to gradually decrease the contribution to the Union target set in Article 3(1) and to the minimum share referred to in the first subparagraph of Article 25(1), of high indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels produced from feedstock for which a significant expansion of the production into land with high-carbon stock is observed.»
- Rules for renewable electricity used to make transport fuels (date passed). «By 31 December 2021, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 35 to supplement this Directive by establishing a Union methodology setting out detailed rules by which economic operators are to comply with the requirements laid down in the fifth and sixth subparagraphs of this paragraph.»
- Savings methodology for fuels made with fossil fuels in a common process (date passed). «By 31 December 2021, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 35 to supplement this Directive by specifying the methodology to determine the share of biofuel, and biogas for transport, resulting from biomass being processed with fossil fuels in a common process»
- Thresholds for recycled carbon fuels (date passed). «By 1 January 2021, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 35 to supplement this Directive by establishing appropriate minimum thresholds for greenhouse gas emissions savings of recycled carbon fuels through a life-cycle assessment that takes into account the specificities of each fuel.»

*Analytical inference:* the acts whose spans say so (certification of low-risk fuels, thresholds for recycled carbon fuels, rules for renewable electricity used to make transport fuels, the savings methodology, and the feedstock list review) concern which fuels count toward the share or how their savings are measured, and so what a fuel supplier can sell as counting toward the obligation; the assessments and the review report state no such change. The text states no cost effect on a freight business. The sections of this document most likely to change when a step is adopted are sections 7, 8 and 12.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a fuel counts at all: what the sustainability criteria cover. «Energy from biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels shall be taken into account for the purposes referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of this subparagraph only if they fulfil the sustainability and the greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in paragraphs 2 to 7 and 10: (a) contributing towards the Union target set in Article 3(1) and the renewable energy shares of Member States; (b) measuring compliance with renewable energy obligations, including the obligation laid down in Article 25; (c) eligibility for financial support for the consumption of biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels.»

For waste and residues the test is narrower: «biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels produced from waste and residues, other than agricultural, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry residues, are required to fulfil only the greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in paragraph 10 in order to be taken into account for the purposes referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of the first subparagraph.»

For biomass fuels the criteria apply by the size of the installation: «Biomass fuels shall fulfil the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in paragraphs 2 to 7 and 10 if used in installations producing electricity, heating and cooling or fuels with a total rated thermal input equal to or exceeding 20 MW in the case of solid biomass fuels, and with a total rated thermal input equal to or exceeding 2 MW in the case of gaseous biomass fuels.» They do not depend on origin: «The sustainability and the greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in paragraphs 2 to 7 and 10 shall apply irrespective of the geographical origin of the biomass.»

*Analytical inference:* a fuel made from waste or residue of the kinds that span covers meets only the greenhouse gas saving test, while agricultural, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry residues, which the span leaves out, and fuels made from crops meet the wider set; so the feedstock named on a supplier's proof settles which test applies. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which category a particular fuel and its feedstock fall into under the national law that carries this Directive.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Union target. «Member States shall collectively ensure that the share of energy from renewable sources in the Union's gross final consumption of energy in 2030 is at least 32 %.»

Transport share carried by fuel suppliers. «each Member State shall set an obligation on fuel suppliers to ensure that the share of renewable energy within the final consumption of energy in the transport sector is at least 14 % by 2030 (minimum share) in accordance with an indicative trajectory set by the Member State and calculated in accordance with the methodology set out in this Article and in Articles 26 and 27.» Stored date form: 1 January 2030, the first day of the year 2030 for which the text sets that minimum share, an obligation level and not a day by which a freight business must act. Within it, a smaller share is set for advanced biofuels and biogas, whose 2022 and 2025 steps have passed and whose 2030 step is ahead: «the contribution of advanced biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part A of Annex IX as a share of final consumption of energy in the transport sector shall be at least 0,2 % in 2022, at least 1 % in 2025 and at least 3,5 % in 2030.» Governments may choose who is covered: «Member States may exempt, or distinguish between, different fuel suppliers and different energy carriers when setting the obligation on the fuel suppliers, ensuring that the varying degrees of maturity and the cost of different technologies are taken into account.» Renewable liquid and gaseous transport fuels of non-biological origin have their own saving test, in force since the date in the quote: «The greenhouse gas emissions savings from the use of renewable liquid and gaseous transport fuels of non-biological origin shall be at least 70 % from 1 January 2021.»

Limits on crop-based fuels. «the share of biofuels and bioliquids, as well as of biomass fuels consumed in transport, where produced from food and feed crops, shall be no more than one percentage point higher than the share of such fuels in the final consumption of energy in the road and rail transport sectors in 2020 in that Member State, with a maximum of 7 % of final consumption of energy in the road and rail transport sectors in that Member State.» A second limit applies to fuels from crops linked to land with high carbon stock, and it is already falling toward zero (the fall started on the first date in the quote, which has passed): «the share of high indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids or biomass fuels produced from food and feed crops for which a significant expansion of the production area into land with high-carbon stock is observed shall not exceed the level of consumption of such fuels in that Member State in 2019, unless they are certified to be low indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids or biomass fuels pursuant to this paragraph. From 31 December 2023 until 31 December 2030 at the latest, that limit shall gradually decrease to 0 %.» A limit also applies to the feedstocks of Part B of Annex IX («Part B. Feedstocks for the production of biofuels and biogas for transport, the contribution of which towards the minimum share established in the first subparagraph of Article 25(1) shall be limited and may be considered to be twice their energy content: (a) Used cooking oil; (b) Animal fats classified as categories 1 and 2 in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009.»): «the share of biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part B of Annex IX shall, except for in Cyprus and Malta, be limited to 1,7 % of the energy content of transport fuels supplied for consumption or use on the market. Member States may, where justified, modify that limit, taking into account the availability of feedstock. Any such modification shall be subject to approval by the Commission;»

How fuels are counted. «(a) the share of biofuels and biogas for transport produced from the feedstock listed in Annex IX may be considered to be twice its energy content; (b) the share of renewable electricity shall be considered to be four times its energy content when supplied to road vehicles and may be considered to be 1,5 times its energy content when supplied to rail transport; (c) with the exception of fuels produced from food and feed crops, the share of fuels supplied in the aviation and maritime sectors shall be considered to be 1,2 times their energy content.» *Analytical inference:* the same amount of energy counts for more than its physical size when it is waste-based advanced fuel, renewable electricity or aviation and maritime fuel other than fuel made from food and feed crops, so a supplier can reach the share with less physical fuel of those kinds; the text states no price or rate effect of this.

Proof of sustainability. The counting test is quoted in section 7. The saving thresholds, in which the dates up to 1 January 2026 have passed: «The greenhouse gas emission savings from the use of biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels taken into account for the purposes referred to in paragraph 1 shall be: (a) at least 50 % for biofuels, biogas consumed in the transport sector, and bioliquids produced in installations in operation on or before 5 October 2015; (b) at least 60 % for biofuels, biogas consumed in the transport sector, and bioliquids produced in installations starting operation from 6 October 2015 until 31 December 2020; (c) at least 65 % for biofuels, biogas consumed in the transport sector, and bioliquids produced in installations starting operation from 1 January 2021; (d) at least 70 % for electricity, heating and cooling production from biomass fuels used in installations starting operation from 1 January 2021 until 31 December 2025, and 80 % for installations starting operation from 1 January 2026.» The proof is shown through a mass balance system, and each consignment carries its support record: «shall include information on whether support has been provided for the production of that consignment, and if so, on the type of support scheme.» Independent checking is required: «Member States shall require economic operators to arrange for an adequate standard of independent auditing of the information submitted, and to provide evidence that this has been done.» The obligations of that paragraph cover imports too: «The obligations laid down in this paragraph shall apply regardless of whether the biofuels, bioliquids, biomass fuels, renewable liquid and gaseous transport fuels of non-biological origin, or recycled carbon fuels are produced within the Union or are imported.»

Tracing database. «The Commission shall ensure that a Union database is put in place to enable the tracing of liquid and gaseous transport fuels that are eligible for being counted towards the numerator referred to in point (b) of Article 27(1) or that are taken into account for the purposes referred to in points (a), (b), and (c) of the first subparagraph of Article 29(1).» «Member States shall require the relevant economic operators to enter into that database information on the transactions made and the sustainability characteristics of those fuels, including their life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions, starting from their point of production to the fuel supplier that places the fuel on the market.»

Customer-facing information. «Information about the geographic origin and feedstock type of biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels per fuel supplier shall be made available to consumers on the websites of operators, suppliers or the relevant competent authorities and shall be updated on an annual basis.»

Penalty. No penalty: the text of the Directive states no penalty, fine or sanction. *Analytical inference:* the Directive is addressed to the Member States (section 1), so any penalty for a fuel supplier or an economic operator sits in the national law that carries the Directive, which is not in the text read here.

*Cause and effect, as far as the text states it:* the cause is the obligation on fuel suppliers; its mechanical consequence is that only fuels meeting the counting, limit and proof rules count toward the share; the effect on a freight business, by cargo type or by transport mode, is not stated and needs supplier-specific and contract-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a fuel supplier's cost of meeting the transport obligation can be charged on to a freight business under its supply or transport contracts, and which party in a fuel chain is the fuel supplier under the national law.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Directive sets duties for Member States, fuel suppliers and economic operators and classifies no product that a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Fuel suppliers enter data in the tracing database: «Fuel suppliers shall enter the information necessary to verify compliance with the requirements laid down in the first and fourth subparagraphs of Article 25(1) into the relevant database.» Information must be reliable and open to checking: «Member States shall take measures to ensure that economic operators submit reliable information regarding the compliance with the greenhouse gas emissions savings thresholds set in, and adopted pursuant to, Article 25(2), and with the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in Article 29(2) to (7) and (10), and that economic operators make available to the relevant Member State, upon request, the data that were used to develop the information.» Member States had to bring the Directive into national law and tell the Commission the text, by a date that has passed: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Articles 2 to 13, 15 to 31 and 37 and Annexes II, III and V to IX, by 30 June 2021.»

The text sets no format and no filing date for the database entries and names no registration of a freight business. *Analytical inference:* a freight business has no registration or filing duty under these articles; what reaches it is a request for proof from a supplier or customer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national law adds a registration for businesses that sell renewable-fuel claims.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive asks a freight business to build nothing directly. The systems it names sit with Member States and operators: «requires information about the sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions saving characteristics and sizes of the consignments referred to in point (a) to remain assigned to the mixture;» Member States also had to see to fuel availability and recharging, by a date that has passed: «By 31 December 2021, Member States shall take measures to ensure the availability of fuels from renewable sources for transport including with regard to publicly accessible high-power recharging points and other refuelling infrastructure as provided for in their national policy frameworks in accordance with Directive 2014/94/EU.»

- A data lead adds, at the next supplier onboarding, a field for fuel type and feedstock to the supplier record, so that the supplier's proof can be matched to a shipment.
- A quote desk keeps, per shipment that carries a renewable-fuel claim, the supplier's proof reference with the quote record, from the next quote that offers such a claim.

*Analytical inference:* the gap between a normal supplier record and the proof the Directive describes is a missing link between a fuel consignment and its sustainability data; the text states no deadline for a freight business to close it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a customer may require this link from a forwarder by contract.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Several exemptions and edge cases sit in the text. Governments may exempt suppliers of some fuels: «Member States may exempt fuel suppliers supplying fuel in the form of electricity or renewable liquid and gaseous transport fuels of non-biological origin from the requirement to comply with the minimum share of advanced biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part A of Annex IX with respect to those fuels.» Waste and residue fuels face only one of the tests: «biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels produced from waste and residues, other than agricultural, aquaculture, fisheries and forestry residues, are required to fulfil only the greenhouse gas emissions saving criteria laid down in paragraph 10 in order to be taken into account for the purposes referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of the first subparagraph.» The 1,7 % limit on Part B feedstocks does not apply in two Member States: «the share of biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part B of Annex IX shall, except for in Cyprus and Malta, be limited to 1,7 % of the energy content of transport fuels supplied for consumption or use on the market. Member States may, where justified, modify that limit, taking into account the availability of feedstock. Any such modification shall be subject to approval by the Commission;»

*Analytical inference:* these carve-outs mean the same fuel can be treated differently from one Member State to another; a freight business should not assume that a claim accepted in one country is accepted in another. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which exemption a given supplier relies on under national law.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 11 December 2018: Directive adopted at Strasbourg (in force)
- 24 December 2018: the Commission's five-year delegation of powers to adopt delegated acts starts from this date (in force)
- 1 February 2019: Commission report on crop expansion and delegated act on certification of low-risk fuels (date passed)
- 25 June 2019: first Commission review of the Part A and Part B feedstock list, then every two years (date passed)
- 31 December 2020: Commission review of guidelines for the calculation of land carbon stocks (date passed)
- 1 January 2021: each Member State's baseline share applies; 70 % saving for fuels of non-biological origin; Commission act on recycled carbon fuels due (date passed)
- 31 January 2021: Commission implementing acts on forest biomass evidence due (date passed)
- 30 June 2021: Member States' deadline to bring the Directive into force in national law (date passed)
- 1 July 2021: earlier renewable energy directive repealed (date passed)
- 31 December 2021: Member State measures on fuel and recharging availability; Commission delegated acts on renewable fuels (date passed)
- 1 September 2023: Commission review of the low-risk certification criteria (date passed)
- 31 December 2023: the limit on high-risk crop fuels starts to fall (date passed, in force)
- 31 December 2025: Commission assessment of the advanced biofuels obligation (date passed)
- 1 January 2026: an 80 % saving covers biomass installations starting from that date (in force)
- 31 December 2026: Commission assessments of forest biomass criteria and of extra national criteria
- 31 December 2030: the limit on high-risk crop fuels reaches 0 % at the latest

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/884 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 March 2024 amending Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE)» It is an act of the European Union, «Done at Strasbourg, 13 March 2024.» The Directive is «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* because the Directive is addressed to the Member States, its duties sit with the national authorities and with the producers they bind, and a freight business meets it through its customers. The Directive names no forwarder, carrier or shipper. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. Section 6 states the Directive's dated review.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive changes who pays for the collection and treatment of waste from two groups of products, photovoltaic panels and the equipment the text calls open-scope EEE, and it dates the mark of the date of placing on the market (Article 15(2)) for them. What it does: «Article 1 Amendments to Directive 2012/19/EU Directive 2012/19/EU is amended as follows» Why: «the Court of Justice of the European Union (the ‘Court’), in its judgment in Case C-181/20 ( 5 ) , declared Article 13(1) of Directive 2012/19/EU to be invalid in so far as it concerns photovoltaic panels placed on the market between 13 August 2005 and 13 August 2012, by reason of non-justified retroactive effect» What applies instead: «Articles 8 and 14 of Directive 2008/98/EC therefore apply to the management of waste from photovoltaic panels and of waste from open-scope EEE for the period when photovoltaic panels and open-scope EEE do not fall within the scope of Directive 2012/19/EU by virtue of the amendments to Articles 12 and 13 thereof by this Directive» For photovoltaic panels, before Directive 2012/19/EU, Member States had a choice: «the Union legislature left Member States the choice of requiring the costs relating to the management of waste from photovoltaic panels to be borne by current or previous waste holders or by the producer or distributor of the photovoltaic panels, pursuant to Article 14 of Directive 2008/98/EC» When it starts: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

*Analytical inference:* the amendments take photovoltaic panels placed on the market before 13 August 2012 and open-scope EEE placed on the market before 15 August 2018 out of the producer financing duties of Directive 2012/19/EU, so a freight business meets the Directive where a customer makes or sells such products, or holds waste from them. The text names no transport mode, route or freight service and states no freight cost.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that places photovoltaic panels or other electrical and electronic equipment on the market under its own name is a producer for the amended Articles 12 to 15, which this text does not say.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Member State deadline has passed: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 9 October 2025» The captured text does not say which Member States have brought the Directive into force. The next dated step is the Commission's assessment no later than 31 December 2026 (section 6). Two steps a freight desk can start now:

- A compliance lead asks each customer that sends waste photovoltaic panels or other waste electrical and electronic equipment for collection or treatment in the European Union which party pays for the collection and treatment under the national rule of the Member State concerned, and records the answer on the customer file before quoting that movement.
- A sales lead asks each customer that ships photovoltaic panels or other electrical and electronic equipment into the Union which cut-off its goods fall under, 13 August 2012 for photovoltaic panels or 15 August 2018 for the equipment of Article 2(1), point (b), and whether the goods carry the Annex IX symbol of Article 14(4) and the mark of the date of placing on the market of Article 15(2), which starts at that cut-off for goods placed on the market, and records the answer with the booking.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: the Member States, the Commission, producers, distributors, current or previous waste holders, private households and users other than private households. «Each producer shall be responsible for financing the operations referred to in paragraph 1 relating to the waste from his own products. The producer may choose to fulfil this obligation either individually or by joining a collective scheme.» The text names no forwarder, carrier, importer or customs broker, and states no rule on what a freight business records for these goods.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is in the chain through its customers: a customer that is a producer finances the waste operations of its own products, and a customer that holds older waste may be a waste holder in the sense of the choice quoted in section 2.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that moves these goods, or the waste from them, falls into any of the named roles in the Member States it serves, which the text does not say.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text is the Directive itself, and no separate authoritative guidance document on it is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets one dated step ahead. «No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall assess the need for a revision of this Directive and, where appropriate, present a legislative proposal in that respect, accompanied by a thorough socioeconomic and environmental impact assessment» The impact assessment is to consider, among other points: «(d) provisions which ensure full implementation and enforcement of this Directive, in particular with regard to adequate collection targets, as well as with regard to preventing illegal trade of WEEE» «(e) creating a new EEE category for ‘photovoltaic panels’ under this Directive with the aim to disassociate photovoltaic panels from the existing EEE category 4, ‘large equipment’, as referred to in Annexes III and IV, and calculating the collection targets on the basis of waste photovoltaic panels available for collection based on their expected lifetime, rather than on the quantity of products placed on the market» «(f) establishing a mechanism to ensure that, in the event of failure or liquidation of the producer, the future costs of collection, treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal of waste from photovoltaic panels from both private households and users other than private households will be covered financially»

*Analytical inference:* the assessment could lead to a proposal that changes collection targets, the treatment of photovoltaic panels as their own category and the financing of their waste if a producer fails; the text lists these as points to consider and states no outcome. The text names preventing illegal trade of WEEE among the points to assess and does not say what a proposal would require.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission has presented the assessment or a proposal, and what a proposal would require of the customers that move or hold these goods, which this text does not say.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: which cut-off a product falls under decides who finances its waste and when the Article 15(2) mark is required. The text defines the second group: «EEE which did not fall within the scope of Directive 2012/19/EU pursuant to Article 2(1), point (a), thereof but which fell within its scope as from 15 August 2018 pursuant to Article 2(1), point (b), thereof (‘open-scope EEE’)»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given product is a photovoltaic panel or open-scope EEE, and so which cut-off date applies to it, which this text does not decide.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Directive amends the producer financing and marking duties of Directive 2012/19/EU; the changes bind whoever the Member States bind through those articles. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Scope of the earlier Directive: «Article 2(1), point (b), of Directive 2012/19/EU extends the scope of application of that Directive to all EEE as from 15 August 2018»

Financing, private households: «1. Member States shall ensure that producers provide at least for the financing of the collection, treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal of WEEE from private households that has been deposited at collection facilities set up under Article 5(2) as follows: (a) for WEEE resulting from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (a), other than photovoltaic panels, where such EEE was placed on the market after 13 August 2005; (b) for WEEE resulting from photovoltaic panels where such photovoltaic panels were placed on the market from 13 August 2012; and (c) for WEEE resulting from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (b), and which does not fall within the scope of Article 2(1), point (a), where such EEE was placed on the market from 15 August 2018»

Financing, users other than private households: «1. Member States shall ensure that the financing of the costs for the collection, treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal of WEEE from users other than private households is to be provided for by producers as follows: (a) for WEEE resulting from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (a), other than photovoltaic panels, where such EEE was placed on the market after 13 August 2005; (b) for WEEE resulting from photovoltaic panels where such photovoltaic panels were placed on the market from 13 August 2012; and (c) for WEEE resulting from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (b), which does not fall within the scope of Article 2(1), point (a), where such EEE was placed on the market from 15 August 2018» Historical waste: «For historical waste from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (a), other than photovoltaic panels, being replaced by new equivalent products or by new products fulfilling the same function, the financing of the costs shall be provided for by producers of those products when supplying them. Member States may, as an alternative, provide that users other than private households also be made, partly or totally, responsible for that financing. For other historical waste from EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (a), other than photovoltaic panels, the financing of the costs shall be provided for by the users other than private households»

*Analytical inference:* resting on the amended Articles 12 and 13, a photovoltaic panel placed on the market before 13 August 2012 and open-scope EEE placed on the market before 15 August 2018 are in none of the three producer financing cases, and section 2 gives the Directive that applies to their waste instead. The text states no amount, and no pass-through to a freight charge.

Marking: «Member States shall ensure that producers appropriately mark – preferably in accordance with the European standard EN 50419:2022 – EEE placed on the market with the symbol shown in Annex IX» Dating the mark: «For photovoltaic panels, the obligation referred to in the first subparagraph shall only apply to photovoltaic panels placed on the market from 13 August 2012. For EEE referred to in Article 2(1), point (b), and which do not fall within the scope of Article 2(1), point (a), the obligation referred to in the first subparagraph of this paragraph shall only apply to the EEE placed on the market from 15 August 2018»

*Analytical inference:* resting on the amended Article 15(2), the duty of the mark that specifies the date of placing on the market starts later for the two groups: from 13 August 2012 for photovoltaic panels and from 15 August 2018 for open-scope EEE. The Annex IX symbol of Article 14(4) is quoted above without a cut-off, so the text gives no start date for it.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether, in each Member State a customer ships from or to, the cost of collecting and treating waste from older photovoltaic panels or older equipment falls on the producer, a distributor or the waste holder under the national rule, which this text does not say.

No phase-in is stated in Article 12(1).
No exceptions are stated in Article 12(1).

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

One edge case in the marking duty: «In exceptional cases, where this is necessary because of the size or the function of the product, the symbol shall be printed on the packaging, on the instructions for use and on the warranty of the EEE»

*Analytical inference:* the symbol of Annex IX can appear on the packaging, the instructions for use and the warranty for a product too small or functionally unsuited to carry it, so the mark can sit on the packaging, the instructions for use and the warranty of the product instead of on the product.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which products fall into the size or function case in a given Member State, which the text does not say.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/1785 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 24 April 2024 amending Directive 2010/75/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on industrial emissions (integrated pollution prevention and control) and Council Directive 1999/31/EC on the landfill of waste» It is an act of the European Union, «Done at Strasbourg, 24 April 2024.» The Directive is «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* because the Directive is addressed to the Member States, its duties sit with the national authorities and with the operators of the installations they permit, and a freight business meets it through its customers that run such installations. The Directive names no forwarder, carrier or shipper. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. Section 6 states the Directive's dated reports and reviews.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive revises the Union rules on industrial emissions (Directive 2010/75/EU), which set permit conditions for large industrial installations, and amends the landfill Directive 1999/31/EC. Why: «The Commission announced in the European Green Deal a revision of Union measures to address pollution from large industrial installations, including a review of the sectoral scope of the legislation and how to make it fully consistent with climate, energy and circular economy policies» What it adds to the list of installations: «2.7. Manufacture of batteries, other than exclusively assembling, with a production capacity of 15 000 tonnes of battery cells (cathode, anode, electrolyte, separator, capsule) or more per year» «3.6. Extraction including on-site treatment operations, such as comminution, size control, beneficiation and upgrading, of the following ores on an industrial scale: bauxite, chromium, cobalt, copper, gold, iron, lead, lithium, manganese, nickel, palladium, platinum, tin, tungsten and zinc» It also brings in the rearing of pigs and poultry above capacity thresholds (section 8). When it starts: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

*Analytical inference:* the Directive sets rules for the sites that make, extract and rear goods, not for moving them, so a freight business meets it where a customer runs a battery manufacturing site, an ore extraction site or a pig or poultry rearing site, or a site already covered by Directive 2010/75/EU. The text names no transport mode, route or freight service and states no freight cost.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which customer sites of a freight business fall within the amended Annex I and Annex Ia, which the Directive itself does not say for any named customer.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Directive falls to a freight business within the next month. The Member State deadline has passed: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 1 July 2026» The captured text does not say which Member States have brought the Directive into force. The first operator date ahead is «The operator shall prepare and implement the EMS in accordance with the relevant BAT conclusions for the sector by 1 July 2027, except for installations referred to in Article 3(4) of Directive (EU) 2024/1785» Two steps a freight desk can start now:

- A compliance lead asks each customer that runs an industrial site in the European Union, such as the manufacture of batteries, the extraction of the listed ores, the rearing of pigs or poultry above the Annex Ia thresholds, or an installation already under Directive 2010/75/EU, whether the site falls within the Directive and what its permit update date is, and records the answer on the customer file before 1 July 2027.
- A network planning lead asks each such customer how it would tell the desk if its competent authority suspends the operation of its installation, and records that contact on the booking file for the site.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: the Member States, the competent authority, the operator of an installation, natural or legal persons subject to obligations, the Commission and an audit organisation. «Member States shall require the operator to prepare and implement, for each installation falling within the scope of this Chapter, an environmental management system» «They shall also adopt compliance assurance measures to promote, monitor and enforce compliance with obligations placed on natural or legal persons under this Directive»

The text names no forwarder, carrier, importer or customs broker, and states no rule on what a freight business records for goods from these sites.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is in the chain through its customers: a customer that is the operator of an installation carries the duties in section 8, and a freight business is not an operator unless it runs an installation of its own.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that runs an installation of the listed activities of its own is an operator under the amended Directive, which the text does not say.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text is the Directive itself, and no separate authoritative guidance document on it is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets dated steps for the Commission. Next in time: «The Commission shall, using an evidence-based methodology and taking into account the specificities of the sector, assess the need for Union action to: (a) comprehensively address the emissions from the rearing of livestock within the Union, in particular from cattle; and (b) further achieve the objective of global environmental protection with respect to products placed on the Union market, through the prevention and control of emissions from livestock farming, and in a manner consistent with the Union’s international obligations. The Commission shall report the results of that assessment by 31 December 2026 to the European Parliament and the Council. The report shall be accompanied by a legislative proposal where appropriate» Later:

- Implementation report: «By 30 June 2028 and every 5 years thereafter, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report reviewing the implementation of this Directive»
- Reviews in that report: «4. The Commission shall review: (a) the need to control emissions from onshore and offshore exploration and production of mineral oil and gas; (b) the need to control emissions from the on-site treatment and extraction of non-energy industrial minerals used in industry other than for construction, as well as the need to control emissions from the on-site treatment and extraction of ores which are newly carried out in the Union; (c) the need to revise the activity threshold in Annex I for the production of hydrogen by electrolysis of water. The Commission shall include the results of that review in the first of the reports to the European Parliament and to the Council required under the first paragraph»
- Guidelines on a single unit: «By 5 August 2028, the Commission shall publish guidelines, after consulting the Member States, on the criteria for considering different installations to be a single unit under paragraph 1»
- Review of the delegated act: «The Commission shall, by 31 December 2034, review and, where appropriate, revise the delegated act referred to in the first subparagraph»

Dates that have passed on the date of this document:

- Delegated powers: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 27d, Article 48(5), and Article 74 shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of 5 years from 1 August 2024»

- EMS information: «The Commission shall, by 31 December 2025, adopt an implementing act on which information is relevant for publication»
- Transformation plans: «The Commission shall, by 30 June 2026, adopt a delegated act in order to supplement this Directive by specifying the content for the transformation plans»
- Compliance assessment: «The Commission shall by 1 September 2026 adopt an implementing act establishing the method for assessing compliance under normal operating conditions with emission limit values set out in the permit with regard to emissions to air and water»
- Livestock operating rules: «The Commission shall adopt by 1 September 2026 an implementing act to establish uniform conditions for operating rules for each of the activities referred to in Annex Ia»

The captured text does not say whether the acts due on those dates have been adopted.

*Analytical inference:* the implementing and delegated acts fix what an operator publishes, how compliance with emission limit values is assessed and what the transformation plans contain, so they set the detail of the duties in section 8. The text states no effect on freight charges.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the acts due on the dates that have passed have been adopted, and what they require of the customer sites of a freight business.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: for pig and poultry rearing, are neighbouring installations counted as one for the capacity threshold? The text answers: «if two or more installations engaged in livestock rearing activities are located close to each other and if their operator is the same or if the installations are under the control of operators who are engaged in an economic or legal relationship, the competent authority may consider those installations to be a single unit for the purpose of calculating the capacity threshold referred to in Article 70a»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a customer's installations are a single unit for the Annex Ia thresholds, which the Directive leaves to the competent authority and to the guidelines of the Commission.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Directive sets permit, management and reporting duties on operators through Member States, and penalty and process duties on Member States. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Livestock rearing. «Installations fall within the scope of this annex if they fall within one or more of the following activity categories: 1. Rearing of pigs representing 350 LSU or more, excluding rearing activities that are carried out under organic production regimes in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/848, or where the stocking density is less than 2 LSU/hectare used only for grazing or growing fodder or forage used for feeding the animals and the animals are reared outside for a significant amount of time in a year or seasonally reared outside» «Rearing of only laying hens representing 300 LSU or more, or rearing of only other poultry categories representing 280 LSU or more»

Environmental management system. «The EMS shall include at least the following: (a) environmental policy objectives for the continuous improvement of the environmental performance and safety of the installation, which shall include measures to: (i) prevent the generation of waste; (ii) optimise resource and energy use and water reuse; (iii) prevent or reduce the use or emissions of hazardous substances» «(d) a chemicals inventory of the hazardous substances present in or emitted from the installation as such, as constituents of other substances or as part of mixtures» «The EMS shall be audited for the first time by 1 July 2027 except for installations referred to in Article 3(4) of Directive (EU) 2024/1785. The EMS shall be audited at least every 3 years»

Transformation plans. «Member States shall require that operators by 30 June 2030 include in their EMS an indicative transformation plan covering their activities as listed in points 1, 2, 3, 4, 6.1 a, and 6.1 b of Annex I. The transformation plan shall contain information on how the operator will transform the installation during the 2030-2050 period to contribute to the emergence of a sustainable, clean, circular, resource-efficient and climate-neutral economy by 2050» «Member States shall require that, as part of the review of the permit conditions pursuant to Article 21(3) following the publication of decisions on BAT conclusions after 1 January 2030, the operator includes in its EMS a transformation plan for each installation carrying out any activity listed in Annex I that is not referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article» «The operator shall make its transformation plan, updates of the transformation plan, as well as the results of the assessment referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 public»

*Analytical inference:* resting on Article 14a and Article 27d as amended, and subject to the transitional dates in section 12, an operator that is a customer of a freight business must have a management system and, for the activities listed, a published plan for 2030 to 2050; the text sets no duty on a freight business and states no cost.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Directive sets transitional dates that move when new duties reach a site. «In relation to installations carrying out activities referred to in Annex I which fall within the scope of the Directive before 4 August 2024 and that are in operation and hold a permit before 1 July 2026, Article 14(1), second subparagraph, points (a), (b), (ba), and (d), and Article 15(1), Article 15(5), Article 15a and Article 16(4) shall apply when the permit is granted or updated pursuant to Article 20(2) or Article 21(5), or updated within 4 years of publication of decisions on BAT conclusions that have been published after 1 July 2026 in accordance with Article 13(5) relating to the main activity of an installation, or by 1 September 2036, whichever is the earlier» «In relation to installations which do not fall within the scope of Directive 2010/75/EU before 4 August 2024 and carrying out activities referred to in Annex I, points 1.4, 2.3(b), 2.3(ba), 2.7 and 3.6, Member States shall, with the exception of Article 14(1), second subparagraph, points (aa), (bb), and (h), Article 15(4) and Article 15(6), apply the laws, regulations and administrative provisions adopted in accordance with this Directive within 4 years of publication of decisions on BAT conclusions in accordance with Article 13(5) relating to the main activity of an installation or by 1 September 2034, whichever is the earlier»

*Analytical inference:* the outer date is earlier for installations outside the Directive's scope before 4 August 2024 in the listed points, which include 2.7 and 3.6 quoted in section 2, than for installations already in scope, so a battery manufacturing or ore extraction customer that was outside the scope before that date reaches the listed provisions by the earlier outer date at the latest; the text does not say for which sites that is the case.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which transitional date applies to a given customer site, which depends on whether the site fell within Directive 2010/75/EU before 4 August 2024 and which the text does not decide.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/2881 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 October 2024 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe (recast)» It is an act of the European Union, «Done at Strasbourg, 23 October 2024.» The Directive is «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* because the Directive is addressed to the Member States, its duties are set on the national authorities, and a freight business meets it through the plans, zones and rules each Member State adopts. The Directive names no forwarder, carrier or shipper as a duty holder. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. Section 6 states the Directive's scheduled review.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive sets European Union air quality standards for pollutants such as particulate matter and nitrogen dioxide, and replaces two older air quality directives. What it sets: «This Directive lays down limit values, target values, average exposure reduction obligations, average exposure concentration objectives, critical levels, alert thresholds, information thresholds and long-term objectives.» Why: «so that air quality within the Union is progressively improved to levels no longer considered harmful to human health, natural ecosystems or biodiversity, cannot be sufficiently achieved by the Member States by reason of the transboundary nature of air pollutants, but can rather, by reason of its scale and effects, be better achieved at Union level, the Union may adopt measures, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in Article 5 of the Treaty on European Union. In accordance with the principle of proportionality as set out in that Article, this Directive does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve that objective, HAVE ADOPTED THIS DIRECTIVE: CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS Article 1 Objectives 1. This Directive sets out air quality provisions with the aim of achieving a zero-pollution objective, so that air quality within the Union is progressively improved to levels no longer considered harmful to human health, natural ecosystems and biodiversity, as defined by the best available and most up-to-date scientific evidence, thus contributing to a toxic-free environment at the latest by 2050.» What it replaces: «Directives 2004/107/EC and 2008/50/EC, as amended by the acts listed in Part A of Annex XI to this Directive, are repealed with effect from 12 December 2026» When it starts: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» Part of it applies later: «Article 13(4), Article 14, Article 16(3), Article 17(1), (2) and (3) and Article 22(4) shall apply from 12 December 2026»

Where freight comes in: the text names air, water and road transport sources, with airports and ports as examples, when it describes where some measurements are made: «locations where high concentrations of UFP occur that are mainly influenced by sources from air, water or road transport (such as airports, ports or roads), industrial sites or domestic heating»

*Analytical inference:* the Directive measures and limits the air, not the vehicles or the ships, so a freight business is affected where a Member State's plan for a zone that exceeds a limit adds transport measures (section 8). The Directive states no cost, fee or freight rate tied to the standards.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which of a freight business's road, port and airport operations fall under measures a Member State adopts under this Directive, which the Directive itself does not say.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

Standards. «Member States shall ensure that, throughout their zones, levels of pollutants in ambient air do not exceed the respective limit values laid down in Section 1 of Annex I.» The values: air quality roadmap and provided that the conditions set out in paragraph 2 of this Article are met: (a) up to 1 January 2040, if justified by site-specific dispersion characteristics, orographic effective air pollution measures identified in the air quality roadmap, the limit values cannot be attained by the attainment deadline»

*Analytical inference:* the Table 1 values for the calendar year are lower than the Table 2 values (for the calendar year, PM 2,5 at 10 μg/m3 against 25 μg/m3), so a zone that meets today's values but not the Table 1 values is more likely to fall into the plan and roadmap duties below. The text does not name those zones.

Plans and roadmaps. «Where, in given zones, the levels of pollutants in ambient air exceed any limit value or target value laid down in Section 1 of Annex I, Member States shall establish air quality plans for those zones that set out appropriate measures to achieve the limit value or target value concerned and to keep the exceedance period as short as possible, and in any case no longer than 4 years from the end of the calendar year in which the first exceedance was recorded» «Where from 1 January 2026 until 31 December 2029 in a zone or territorial unit, the levels of pollutants are above any limit value or target value to be attained by 1 January 2030 as laid down in Section 1, Table 1, of Annex I and in Section 2, Point B, of Annex I, and without prejudice to paragraph 2, third subparagraph, of this Article, Member States shall establish an air quality roadmap for the pollutant concerned to attain the respective limit values or target values by the expiration of the attainment deadline. Those air quality roadmaps shall be established as soon as possible and no later than 2 years after the calendar year during which the exceedance was recorded. However, Member States may refrain from establishing such air quality roadmaps when the baseline scenario following the information required by Point A, point 5, of Annex VIII, shows that the limit value or target value will be achieved with the measures that are already in force» «(c) information on relevant abatement measures listed in Point B, point 2, of Annex VIII» The measures listed in Annex VIII include these: «(iv) establishing urban vehicles access restrictions schemes, including low emission zones and zero-emission zones» «(vii) ‘last mile’ zero (exhaust) emission delivery arrangements» «(l) reduction of emissions from maritime and air transport through the use of alternative fuels and deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure, as well as the use of economic incentives to accelerate their take-up, and establishing specific requirements for ships and boats at berth and port traffic, while speeding up onshore power supply and electrification of ships and port working machinery»

*Analytical inference:* these three lines are where the Directive lists measures that reach urban vehicle access, last mile delivery, maritime and air transport, ships at berth and port traffic. They are measures a Member State has considered, and the text does not make any of them a duty for a freight business. The text states no cost for these measures and no pass-through to freight charges.

Short-term action plans. «Where, in a given zone, there is a risk that the levels of pollutants will exceed one or more of the alert thresholds specified in Section 4 of Annex I, Member States shall establish short-term action plans indicating the emergency measures to be taken in the short term in order to reduce the risk or duration of such an exceedance» «they shall consider including, where appropriate, in those short-term action plans measures in relation to activities such as transport, construction works, industrial installations, agriculture and the use of products and domestic heating» Annex IX adds: «(a) restricting the circulation of vehicles, specifically around locations frequented by sensitive population and vulnerable groups»

*Analytical inference:* if an alert threshold is at risk in a zone on a lane, a short-term plan could restrict vehicle circulation around locations frequented by sensitive population and vulnerable groups for a short spell; the text sets no duration or fee.

Measurement and exposure. «From 2030, the uncertainty of measurement data used for ambient air quality assessment shall not exceed the absolute value or the relative value, whichever is higher, expressed in this Point» «B. Average exposure reduction obligations As from 2030, the AEI shall not exceed a level that is: 1. for PM 2,5 : (a) when 10 years before the AEI was < 10,0 μg/m 3 : 10 % lower than the AEI was 10 years before or 8,5 μg/m 3 , whichever is the lower, unless the AEI is already no higher than the average exposure concentration objective for PM 2,5 set out in Point C; (b) when 10 years before the AEI was < 12,0 μg/m 3 and ≥ 10,0 μg/m 3 : 15 % lower than the AEI was 10 years before or 9,0 μg/m 3 , whichever is the lower; (c) when 10 years before the AEI was ≥ 12,0 μg/m 3 : 25 % lower than the AEI was 10 years before; 2. for NO 2» A limit on the uncertainty rule: «The uncertainty calculation does not apply to AOT40 and values that include more than 1 year, more than one sampling point (e.g. AEI) or more than one component»

Penalties. «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive» The text names no fine amount and no enforcement body beyond the Member States' own rules.

Access to justice and compensation. «Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with their national legal system, members of the public concerned have access to a review procedure before a court of law, or another independent and impartial body established by law, to challenge the substantive or procedural legality of all decisions, acts or omissions by Member States concerning the location and number of sampling points under Article 9 in accordance with the relevant criteria laid down in Annexes III and IV, air quality plans and air quality roadmaps referred to in Article 19, and short-term action plans referred to in Article 20, of the Member State, provided that any of the following conditions is met: (a) they have a sufficient interest; (b) they maintain the impairment of a right, where administrative procedural law of a Member State requires this as a precondition» «natural persons who suffer damage to human health caused by a violation of the national rules transposing Article 19(1) to (5) and Article 20(1) and (2) of this Directive that has been committed intentionally or negligently by the competent authorities have the right to claim and obtain compensation for that damage»

*Analytical inference:* the penalty rules are national and attach to infringements of national provisions; the compensation sentence runs against competent authorities, not against freight businesses.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given national penalty or measure adopted under this Directive reaches a freight business as an operator, which the Directive does not say.

Member States shall notify the Commission no later than 31 January 2034 where, in their view, attainment cannot be achieved by an attainment deadline postponed in accordance with paragraph 1, second subparagraph»

Natural sources: «Where the Commission has been informed of an exceedance attributable to natural sources in accordance with paragraph 2, that exceedance shall not be considered as an exceedance for the purposes of this Directive»

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 October 2024: Directive done at Strasbourg.
- 10 December 2024: the Commission's power to adopt delegated acts began, for a period of 5 years.

- 11 December 2026: Member State transposition deadline; the Table 2 limit values and Table 3 target values are to be attained.

- 31 December 2026: Commission implementing acts due on natural sources and on winter road treatment.
- 31 January 2029: Member State notice if a postponement is sought.
- 1 January 2030: Table 1 limit values to be attained; from 2030 the uncertainty rule and the average exposure reduction obligations apply.
- 31 December 2030: Commission review and report, then every 5 years.
- 31 January 2034: Member State notice if attainment cannot be achieved by a postponed deadline.
- 1 January 2035: a general decreasing trend is required for a zone under postponement.

The Directive enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication; the text gives no other entry date.
