   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/1760 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 on corporate sustainability due diligence», the European Union's directive on corporate sustainability due diligence. A directive is a law addressed to governments, which each write it into national law; it reaches a business through that national law. Where it applies: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» What it covers: «This Directive lays down rules on: (a) obligations for companies regarding actual and potential human rights adverse impacts and environmental adverse impacts, with respect to their own operations, the operations of their subsidiaries, and the operations carried out by their business partners in the chains of activities of those companies;»

The text read here is the Directive as adopted. It holds no later amendment, so any later act that changes its dates or its size thresholds is not covered here, and every date below is the date this adopted text states. What the Directive says is quoted from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The text names no freight forwarder, so each statement about a forwarder's position is a reading and not something the text says. This document serves the regulatory and operational lenses from the Directive's own text. The text holds no market price and no research study, so it carries no market or research content.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

In plain terms, the Directive makes large companies find, stop and put right harm to people and to the environment, not only in their own operations but across the partners that work for them. Which companies are covered is set mainly by size, with other conditions for groups and for franchising and licensing royalties. The first test, for companies formed in a Member State: «This Directive shall apply to companies which are formed in accordance with the legislation of a Member State and which fulfil one of the following conditions: (a) the company had more than 1 000 employees on average and had a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 450 000 000 in the last financial year for which annual financial statements have been or should have been adopted;» For a company formed outside the Union, a turnover test in the Union applies: «This Directive shall also apply to companies which are formed in accordance with the legislation of a third country and fulfil one of the following conditions: (a) the company generated a net turnover of more than EUR 450 000 000 in the Union in the financial year preceding the last financial year;» Size must hold for a stretch of time: «Where a company meets the conditions laid down in paragraph 1 or 2, this Directive shall only apply if those conditions are met in two consecutive financial years.»

When it took effect: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» The title gives the adoption date as 13 June 2024. The Directive also reaches climate planning: «(c) the obligation for companies to adopt and put into effect a transition plan for climate change mitigation which aims to ensure, through best efforts, compatibility of the business model and of the strategy of the company with the transition to a sustainable economy»

How it reaches a freight business: the Directive counts transport and storage partners inside a company's chain of activities (section 7). *Analytical inference:* a freight business is reached as a business partner of a covered company, which must ask its partners for assurances and information (sections 4 and 8), and reached directly only if it is itself a covered company above the size tests. The text states no price or rate effect, so what a covered company's requests cost a freight business, or what the business can charge for meeting them, is not stated here.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: nothing in the text puts a step on a freight business in the coming month. The first company compliance date in the text falls on the largest covered companies: «They shall apply those measures: (a) from 26 July 2027 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of the Member State and that had more than 5 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 1 500 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2027 for which annual financial statements have been or should have been adopted, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028;» The Commission's nearest step is guidance on model contract clauses: «In order to provide support to companies to facilitate their compliance with Article 10(2), point (b), and Article 11(3), point (c), the Commission, in consultation with Member States and stakeholders, shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contractual clauses, by 26 January 2027.»

- A key-accounts lead asks each large client, at the next account review, whether it falls under the size tests of Article 2, on which date the national rules apply to it, and what it will ask of its transport and storage partners.
- A contracts lead compares, when the Commission's model contract clause guidance is published, the business's standard transport and storage terms with those clauses and lists where a client's code of conduct would add duties.
- A compliance lead checks, at each client meeting that cites a date from this Directive, whether a later act has changed that date, because this document reads the Directive as adopted.
- A data lead writes down, this quarter, the sites and subcontracted partners that do transport or storage work for each large client, because a covered company may ask for them.

*Analytical inference:* these steps rest on the duties quoted in sections 4 and 8, which fall on covered companies; the Directive requires none of them of a freight business that is not itself covered. The text states no penalty and no cost figure for a freight business that is not itself covered.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The parties the text names are the covered companies, their subsidiaries, their direct and indirect business partners, the Member States, the supervisory authorities, the Commission and an authorised representative for companies formed outside the Union. A forwarder is not named. Business partners are defined as follows: «‘business partner’ means an entity: (i) with which the company has a commercial agreement related to the operations, products or services of the company or to which the company provides services pursuant to point (g) (‘direct business partner’); or (ii) which is not a direct business partner but which performs business operations related to the operations, products or services of the company (‘indirect business partner’);»

A covered company is to ask its direct partners for assurances: «(b) seek contractual assurances from a direct business partner that it will ensure compliance with the company’s code of conduct and, as necessary, a prevention action plan, including by establishing corresponding contractual assurances from its partners, to the extent that their activities are part of the company’s chain of activities; when such contractual assurances are obtained, paragraph 5 shall apply;» It is to check them: «The contractual assurances referred to in paragraph 2, point (b), and in paragraph 4, shall be accompanied by appropriate measures to verify compliance.» For an SME partner the terms must be fair, and the company pays for the checking: «When contractual assurances are obtained from, or a contract is entered into with, an SME, the terms used shall be fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory.» «Where measures to verify compliance are carried out in relation to SMEs, the company shall bear the cost of the independent third-party verification.» A partner need not hand over trade secrets, though the company can still ask for the identity of partners and essential impact information: «Member States shall ensure that a business partner is not obliged to disclose to a company that is complying with the obligations resulting from this Directive information that is a trade secret, as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Directive (EU) 2016/943, without prejudice to the disclosure of the identity of direct and indirect business partners, or essential information needed to identify actual or potential adverse impacts, where necessary and duly justified for the company’s compliance with due diligence obligations.» Where harm cannot be prevented or adequately mitigated, the company may be required, as a last resort, to hold back from new or extended relations with that partner: «the company shall, as a last resort, be required to refrain from entering into new or extending existing relations with a business partner in connection with which, or in the chain of activities of which, the impact has arisen»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that does transport or storage work for a covered company sits as a business partner in that company's chain (section 7), with the covered company asking for assurances, information and verification; the text does not name the freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that arranges transport or storage on behalf of a covered company is a direct or an indirect business partner, and whether it is an SME as the Directive defines the term.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets dated steps for the Commission and the Member States. A date already passed is marked as passed; the text read here does not say whether each step was taken, so the outcome of a passed step is not stated.

Steps ahead:
- Model contract clauses (the Commission). «In order to provide support to companies to facilitate their compliance with Article 10(2), point (b), and Article 11(3), point (c), the Commission, in consultation with Member States and stakeholders, shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contractual clauses, by 26 January 2027.» What it changes for the reader: it fixes the wording a covered company may offer a business partner when it seeks contractual assurances.
- Guidelines (the Commission). «The guidelines referred to in paragraph 2, points (a), (d), and (e), shall be made available by 26 January 2027. The guidelines in paragraph 2, points (b), (f) and (g), shall be made available by 26 July 2027.» What they cover: «(a) guidance and best practices on how to conduct due diligence in accordance with the obligations laid down in Articles 5 to 16, particularly, the identification process pursuant to Article 8, the prioritisation of impacts pursuant to Article 9, appropriate measures to adapt purchasing practices pursuant to Article 10(2) and Article 11(3), responsible disengagement pursuant to Article 10(6) and Article 11(7), appropriate measures for remediation pursuant to Article 12, and on how to identify and engage with stakeholders pursuant to Article 13, including through the notification mechanism and complaints procedure established in Article 14; (b) practical guidance on the transition plan as referred to in Article 22; (c) sector-specific guidance; (d) guidance on the assessment of company-level, business operations, geographic and contextual, product and service, and sectoral risk factors, including those associated with conflict-affected and high-risk areas; (e) references to data and information sources available for the compliance with the obligations provided for in this Directive, and to digital tools and technologies that could facilitate and support compliance; (f) information on how to share resources and information among companies and other legal entities for the purpose of compliance with the provisions of national law adopted pursuant to this Directive, in a manner that is in accordance with the protection of trade secrets pursuant to Article 5(3) and the protection from potential retaliation and retribution as provided for in Article 13(5); (g) information for stakeholders and their representatives on how to engage throughout the due diligence process.» The guidelines due on 26 January 2027 are points (a), (d) and (e): how to conduct due diligence including purchasing practices and remediation, risk factors, and data and information sources; those due on 26 July 2027 are points (b), (f) and (g): the transition plan, sharing of resources and information, and stakeholder engagement.
- Content of the annual statement (the Commission). «By 31 March 2027, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 34 in order to supplement this Directive by laying down the content and criteria for the reporting under paragraph 1, specifying, in particular, sufficiently detailed information on the description of due diligence, actual and potential adverse impacts identified, and appropriate measures taken with respect to those impacts.» What it changes for the reader: it fixes what a covered company says in public about its impacts and measures, which is the information it will gather from its partners.
- Single access point (Member States). «By 31 December 2028, for the purposes of making the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body, as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859, and notify the European Securities and Markets Authority thereof.» «From 1 January 2029, Member States shall ensure that, when making public the annual statement referred to in Article 16(1) of this Directive, companies submit that statement at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)»
- Review report (the Commission). «By 26 July 2030, and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of this Directive and its effectiveness in reaching its objectives, in particular in addressing adverse impacts.»

Steps whose date has passed:
- Delegation of power (date passed). «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 3(2) and Article 16 shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 25 July 2024.»
- National laws and supervisory authorities (date passed). «Member States shall adopt and publish, by 26 July 2026, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.» «By 26 July 2026, Member States shall inform the Commission of the names and contact details of the supervisory authorities designated pursuant to this Article»
- Report on financial undertakings (date passed). «The Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the necessity of laying down additional sustainability due diligence requirements tailored to regulated financial undertakings with respect to the provision of financial services and investment activities, and the options for such due diligence requirements as well as their impacts, in line with the objectives of this Directive. The report shall take into account other Union legislative acts that apply to regulated financial undertakings. It shall be published at the earliest possible opportunity after 25 July 2024, but no later than 26 July 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the model contract clauses, the guidelines and the content of the annual statement are Commission steps that bear on what a covered company will ask of its partners, and the staged dates in section 8 bear on when it starts; the single access point, the review report, the report on financial undertakings and the delegation of power concern none of that. The sections of this document most likely to change from the first three are 4, 8, 10 and 11; the text states no cost effect on a freight business.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Question one: is the business, or a client, a covered company? The size tests are quoted in section 2. Two further rules matter: «Where a company meets the conditions laid down in paragraph 1 or 2, this Directive shall only apply if those conditions are met in two consecutive financial years.» A holding-company parent may be exempted, with a subsidiary designated to carry the duties: «Where the ultimate parent company has as its main activity the holding of shares in operational subsidiaries and does not engage in taking management, operational or financial decisions affecting the group or one or more of its subsidiaries, it may be exempted from carrying out the obligations under this Directive.»

Question two: is a given piece of work inside a company's chain of activities? «‘chain of activities’ means: (i) activities of a company’s upstream business partners related to the production of goods or the provision of services by that company, including the design, extraction, sourcing, manufacture, transport, storage and supply of raw materials, products or parts of products and the development of the product or the service; and (ii) activities of a company’s downstream business partners related to the distribution, transport and storage of a product of that company, where the business partners carry out those activities for the company or on behalf of the company, and excluding the distribution, transport and storage of a product that is subject to export controls under Regulation (EU) 2021/821 or to the export controls relating to weapons, munitions or war materials, once the export of the product is authorised;»

*Analytical inference:* transport and storage done for a covered company, or on its behalf, fall inside its chain of activities, upstream when they form part of making its goods and downstream when they form part of distributing its product, except for the transport and storage of a product subject to the export controls that span names, once its export is authorised. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular movement or storage service falls inside the chain of activities or inside the export-control carve-out.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Due diligence actions. «Member States shall ensure that companies conduct risk-based human rights and environmental due diligence as laid down in Articles 7 to 16 (‘due diligence’) by carrying out the following actions: (a) integrating due diligence into their policies and risk management systems in accordance with Article 7; (b) identifying and assessing actual or potential adverse impacts in accordance with Article 8 and, where necessary, prioritising actual and potential adverse impacts in accordance with Article 9; (c) preventing and mitigating potential adverse impacts, and bringing actual adverse impacts to an end and minimising their extent in accordance with Articles 10 and 11; (d) providing remediation for actual adverse impacts in accordance with Article 12; (e) carrying out meaningful engagement with stakeholders in accordance with Article 13; (f) establishing and maintaining a notification mechanism and a complaints procedure in accordance with Article 14; (g) monitoring the effectiveness of their due diligence policy and measures in accordance with Article 15; (h) publicly communicating on due diligence in accordance with Article 16.»

Policy and code of conduct. «update their due diligence policies without undue delay after a significant change occurs, and review and, where necessary, update such policies at least every 24 months.» The policy contains a code of conduct that reaches partners: «(b) a code of conduct describing rules and principles to be followed throughout the company and its subsidiaries, and the company’s direct or indirect business partners in accordance with Article 10(2), point (b), Article 10(4), Article 11(3), point (c), or Article 11(5);»

Finding harm. «Member States shall ensure that companies take appropriate measures to identify and assess actual and potential adverse impacts arising from their own operations or those of their subsidiaries and, where related to their chains of activities, those of their business partners, in accordance with this Article.» A covered company is to ask partners for information directly: «Where information necessary for the in-depth assessment provided for in paragraph 2, point (b), can be obtained from business partners at different levels of the chain of activities, the company shall prioritise requesting such information, where reasonable, directly from business partners where the adverse impacts are most likely to occur.»

Preventing harm and ending it. «(b) seek contractual assurances from a direct business partner that it will ensure compliance with the company’s code of conduct and, as necessary, a prevention action plan, including by establishing corresponding contractual assurances from its partners, to the extent that their activities are part of the company’s chain of activities; when such contractual assurances are obtained, paragraph 5 shall apply;» «(c) seek contractual assurances from a direct business partner that it will ensure compliance with the company’s code of conduct and, as necessary, a corrective action plan, including by establishing corresponding contractual assurances from its partners, to the extent that their activities are part of the company’s chain of activities; when such contractual assurances are obtained, paragraph 6 shall apply;» Verification follows: «The contractual assurances referred to in paragraph 2, point (b), and in paragraph 4, shall be accompanied by appropriate measures to verify compliance.» For an SME partner: «Where measures to verify compliance are carried out in relation to SMEs, the company shall bear the cost of the independent third-party verification.»

Group-level help. «Member States shall ensure that parent companies falling under the scope of this Directive are allowed to fulfil the obligations set out in Articles 7 to 11 and Article 22 on behalf of companies which are subsidiaries of those parent companies and fall under the scope of this Directive, if this ensures effective compliance.» A holding-company parent may be exempted: «Where the ultimate parent company has as its main activity the holding of shares in operational subsidiaries and does not engage in taking management, operational or financial decisions affecting the group or one or more of its subsidiaries, it may be exempted from carrying out the obligations under this Directive.»

Watching and complaints. «Member States shall ensure that companies carry out periodic assessments of their own operations and measures, those of their subsidiaries and, where related to the chain of activities of the company, those of their business partners, to assess the implementation and to monitor the adequacy and effectiveness of the identification, prevention, mitigation, bringing to an end and minimisation of the extent of adverse impacts. Such assessments shall be based, where appropriate, on qualitative and quantitative indicators and be carried out without undue delay after a significant change occurs, but at least every 12 months» «Member States shall ensure that companies enable persons and entities listed in paragraph 2 to submit complaints to them where those persons or entities have legitimate concerns regarding actual or potential adverse impacts with respect to the companies’ own operations, the operations of their subsidiaries or the operations of their business partners in the chains of activities of the companies.»

Records. «Member States shall require companies to retain documentation regarding the actions carried out to fulfil their due diligence obligations for the purpose of demonstrating compliance, including supporting evidence, for at least 5 years from the moment when such documentation was produced or obtained.»

Public statement. «Member States shall ensure that companies report on the matters covered by this Directive by publishing on their website an annual statement.»

Climate transition plan. «Member States shall ensure that companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a), (b) and (c), and Article 2(2), points (a), (b) and (c), adopt and put into effect a transition plan for climate change mitigation which aims to ensure, through best efforts, that the business model and strategy of the company are compatible with the transition to a sustainable economy» The plan is refreshed: «Member States shall ensure that the transition plan for climate change mitigation referred to in paragraph 1 is updated every 12 months»

Staged application. «They shall apply those measures: (a) from 26 July 2027 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of the Member State and that had more than 5 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 1 500 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2027 for which annual financial statements have been or should have been adopted, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028;» Then: «(b) from 26 July 2028 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of the Member State and that had more than 3 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 900 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2028 for which annual financial statements have been or should have been adopted, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029;» And for companies formed outside the Union: «(c) from 26 July 2027 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(2), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of a third country and that generated a net turnover of more than EUR 1 500 000 000 in the Union, in the financial year preceding the last financial year preceding 26 July 2027, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028; (d) from 26 July 2028 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(2), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of a third country and that generated a net turnover of more than EUR 900 000 000 in the Union, in the financial year preceding the last financial year preceding 26 July 2028, with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029;» And for all others: «(e) from 26 July 2029 as regards all other companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), and Article 2(2), points (a) and (b), and companies referred to in Article 2(1), point (c), and Article 2(2), point (c), with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029.» *Analytical inference:* the dates are staged by size, so the largest covered companies start asking their partners first and a freight business can expect the first requests from the largest clients before the later waves.

Penalty. The Member States set penalties for a covered company's infringements of the national law that carries the Directive: «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties, including pecuniary penalties, applicable to infringements of the provisions of national law adopted pursuant to this Directive, and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» The minimum list: «Member States shall provide for at least the following penalties: (a) pecuniary penalties; (b) if a company fails to comply with a decision imposing a pecuniary penalty within the applicable time limit, a public statement indicating the company responsible for the infringement and the nature of the infringement.» The size of the maximum: «When pecuniary penalties are imposed, they shall be based on the company’s net worldwide turnover. The maximum limit of pecuniary penalties shall be not less than 5 % of the net worldwide turnover of the company in the financial year preceding that of the decision to impose the fine.» Civil liability also applies: «Member States shall ensure that a company can be held liable for damage caused to a natural or legal person, provided that: (a) the company intentionally or negligently failed to comply with the obligations laid down in Articles 10 and 11, when the right, prohibition or obligation listed in the Annex to this Directive is aimed at protecting the natural or legal person; and (b) as a result of the failure referred to in point (a), damage to the natural or legal person’s legal interests that are protected under national law was caused. A company cannot be held liable if the damage was caused only by its business partners in its chain of activities.» *Analytical inference:* these penalties and this liability are set for a covered company; a business partner that is not itself covered is not named as a penalised party in these articles, and the last sentence of the liability span says a company cannot be held liable if the damage was caused only by its business partners.

*Cause and effect, as far as the text states it:* the cause is the duty on a covered company; its mechanical consequence is that it is to seek assurances, information and verification from partners in its chain of activities; the effect on a freight business, by cargo type or by transport mode, is not stated beyond the SME rules above and needs client-specific contract data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a covered company may pass the cost of its due diligence or of verification on to a freight business that is not an SME, and which party bears the cost of a contractual assurance in a transport or storage contract.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The public statement: «Member States shall ensure that companies report on the matters covered by this Directive by publishing on their website an annual statement.» Its submission to the single access point: «From 1 January 2029, Member States shall ensure that, when making public the annual statement referred to in Article 16(1) of this Directive, companies submit that statement at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)» The collection body: «By 31 December 2028, for the purposes of making the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body, as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859, and notify the European Securities and Markets Authority thereof.» Records are kept: «Member States shall require companies to retain documentation regarding the actions carried out to fulfil their due diligence obligations for the purpose of demonstrating compliance, including supporting evidence, for at least 5 years from the moment when such documentation was produced or obtained.» Member States had to tell the Commission of their supervisory authorities, by a date that has passed: «By 26 July 2026, Member States shall inform the Commission of the names and contact details of the supervisory authorities designated pursuant to this Article»

The text sets no registration of a business partner. *Analytical inference:* a freight business that is not itself covered has no registration or filing duty under these articles; what reaches it is a request for information from a covered company. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national law adds a filing for businesses that are covered or that act for a covered company.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive asks a covered company to build the systems; it asks a freight business that is not itself covered for nothing directly, though a covered company may ask that business for information. The systems the text names are: «update their due diligence policies without undue delay after a significant change occurs, and review and, where necessary, update such policies at least every 24 months.» «Member States shall ensure that companies carry out periodic assessments of their own operations and measures, those of their subsidiaries and, where related to the chain of activities of the company, those of their business partners, to assess the implementation and to monitor the adequacy and effectiveness of the identification, prevention, mitigation, bringing to an end and minimisation of the extent of adverse impacts. Such assessments shall be based, where appropriate, on qualitative and quantitative indicators and be carried out without undue delay after a significant change occurs, but at least every 12 months» «Member States shall ensure that companies enable persons and entities listed in paragraph 2 to submit complaints to them where those persons or entities have legitimate concerns regarding actual or potential adverse impacts with respect to the companies’ own operations, the operations of their subsidiaries or the operations of their business partners in the chains of activities of the companies.»

- A systems lead adds, at the next change to the client record, fields for the client's code-of-conduct reference, the date its rules apply and the contact for due diligence requests.
- A complaints lead sets up, at the next review of the business's own policies, a route for a notification or complaint from a client or from affected persons that concerns the business's operations, because the complaints procedure of a covered company can reach the operations of its business partners.

*Analytical inference:* the gap between a normal client record and what a covered company may ask for is missing data on sites, partners and code-of-conduct terms; the text states no date by which a freight business that is not covered must close it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client may require a complaints route or a code-of-conduct clause from a forwarder by contract.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

A holding-company parent may be exempted: «Where the ultimate parent company has as its main activity the holding of shares in operational subsidiaries and does not engage in taking management, operational or financial decisions affecting the group or one or more of its subsidiaries, it may be exempted from carrying out the obligations under this Directive.» Some transport and storage is outside the chain of activities: «‘chain of activities’ means: (i) activities of a company’s upstream business partners related to the production of goods or the provision of services by that company, including the design, extraction, sourcing, manufacture, transport, storage and supply of raw materials, products or parts of products and the development of the product or the service; and (ii) activities of a company’s downstream business partners related to the distribution, transport and storage of a product of that company, where the business partners carry out those activities for the company or on behalf of the company, and excluding the distribution, transport and storage of a product that is subject to export controls under Regulation (EU) 2021/821 or to the export controls relating to weapons, munitions or war materials, once the export of the product is authorised;» The public statement is not required of companies that already report under other sustainability reporting rules: «Paragraph 1 of this Article shall not apply to companies that are subject to sustainability reporting requirements in accordance with Article 19a, 29a or 40a of Directive 2013/34/EU, including those that are exempted in accordance with Article 19a(9) or Article 29a(8) of that Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* the carve-outs mean the same movement can be in or out of a covered company's chain depending on the product and the status of the export. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which carve-out, if any, applies to a given client or shipment.
